P0118.title: Engine Coolant Temperature (ECT) Sensor - Circuit High
P0118.description: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) has detected that the ECT sensor signal is indicating a voltage above 4.91 V (which corresponds to a temperature below -40°C / -40°F).
symptoms: The Check Engine Light (MIL) will illuminate.
Hard starting, especially when the engine is cold.
Poor fuel economy and rich exhaust smell.
Radiator cooling fans may run continuously as a fail-safe measure.
causes: Open or shorted wire in the ECT sensor circuit.
Poor electrical connection or severe corrosion at the ECT connector.
Extremely low engine coolant level (air pocket at the sensor).
howToTestAndFix: Visually inspect the sensor's wiring harness and connector for damage or loose pins.
Use a multimeter to check the sensor's resistance: it should be high when cold and drop as the engine warms up.
Check the harness connector to ensure it is receiving a 5V reference signal from the ECU.
Replace the ECT sensor if its internal resistance is out of factory specifications.
Clear the trouble codes with the scanner and perform a test drive to verify the repair.
